title.narrative: Integrated Response to Drought and conflict affected Communities in Lagahida, Higlooley and Doboweyn Districts of Somali Region, Ethiopia.

description.narrative: ltpgtOWDA, together with RESDO (sub-partner), is proposing a multi-sectoral lifesaving project to provide basic service assistance to people affected by conflict and climatic shocks in Doboweyn and Higloley Woredas in Korahey Zone and Lagahida Woreda in Erer Zone, Somali Region. lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe project's main objectives are:ltbrgt1. To ensure provision of basic services to vulnerable people in hard-to-reach areas affected by different shocks, including drought and conflict. ltbrgt2. To provide critical assistance to internally displaced people to help them recover from shocks and establish sustainable livelihoods.lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtThe project period will be 12 months and will address the most pressing humanitarian needs of the vulnerable communities through a comprehensive, integrated response tailored to the specific needs of the target communities. The project will focus on 4 sectors: WASH, health, nutrition, and agriculture, with protection and gender mainstreamed throughout the project. All the four sectors will be implemented across the three target Woredas, however, specific activities will vary depending on the local context and community needs identified in the assessment. The total proposed budget for this project is 999,999.73 USD allocated for the four sectors as follows: 25% for WASH, 25% for Health, 25% for nutrition, and 25% for agriculture. RESDO, the sub-implementing partner, will manage the agricultural component and will be responsible for 24% of the total budget. RESDO will both contribute to and benefit from this project. With its considerable experience in implementing livelihood in the Somali Region, RESDO is well-positioned to make a meaningful contribution in supporting vulnerable target communities rebuild their livelihoods and recover from past shocks. On the other hand, this project will further strengthen RESDO's capacity to participate more actively in future humanitarian and development intervention that support crisis affected communities.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe project will support 49,530 individuals(without double counting), including 11,392 IDPs and 38,138 host communities. Out of that IDPs 2,278 are women, 3,873 are girls, 2051 are men, and 3,190 are boys. Regarding the host community, 7,628 are women, 12,967 are girls, 6,865 are men, and 10,678 are boys. Beneficiary distribution by Woreda is as follows: 19,812 in Lagahida, 14,875 in Dobowyan, 14,843 in Higloley.lt/pgtltpgtltbgtKey activitieslt/bgtltbrgtltbgtKey WASH activities includelt/bgt: Rehabilitation of Jidhacle borehole by renovating water points, solarization, construction of concrete reservoirs upgrading of Lagahida town borehole construction of two latrines in two health facilities construction of two blocks of communal latrines provision of WASH NFI items for 1,500 HHs and organizing five rounds of hygiene and sanitation campaigns. lt/pgtltpgtltbgtKey Health activities includelt/bgt: Provision of primary healthcare through MHNT training of Public Health Emergency Management officers on Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response training 30 HW/HEWs on IPC establishing and training rapid response teams organizing MISP for 30 MCH heath workers and rehabilitation of two damaged Health facilities. lt/pgtltpgtltbgtKey Nutrition activities includelt/bgt: Supporting routine screening treating SAM and MAM cases, provision of food for care takers Provision of IYCF-E corner materials to HCs, organizing CMAM refresher training to 35 frontline health workers and HEWs and transportation of Nutrition supplies to facilities. lt/pgtltpgtltbgtKey agricilture activities includelt/bgt: procure supplementary feeding for core breeding livestock treat core breeding livestock provide refresher training for the CAHWs support animal mass vaccination campaigns and procure improved crop seeds and farm tools for vulnerable HHs. lt/pgtltpgtltbgtKey cross-cutting activitieslt/bgt: training on PSEA for Project staff training on gender Mainstreaming for key stakeholders provision of MHPSS sessions awareness-raising sessions on gender equality and establish and training of complaint and feedback response committee (CFRM).ltbrgtlt/pgt
